title: Unsupervised Hierarchical Topic Modeling via Anchor Word Clustering and Path Guidance
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024
subcategory: VAE hierarchical topic model guided by anchor words
problem: Neural hierarchical topic models give incoherent or redundant topics and weak parent-child relations because hierarchy construction is not guided by fine-grained word-level semantics.
architecture: AP-HTM: Gaussian-mixture VAE encoder over bag-of-words with layer-wise topic distributions; anchor words obtained by clustering, four causal paths that guide the topic hierarchy, a word co-occurrence graph, and anchor-based contrastive learning.

datasets.name: 20News
datasets.details: benchmark; statistics in the paper's appendix

key_results: NPMI best on all three datasets: NIPS 0.162 vs NG-HTM 0.147, 20News 0.329 vs 0.307, Wikitext-103 0.295 vs 0.255.
TU best on all three (NIPS 0.786, 20News 0.857, Wikitext-103 0.825); TQ best on all three (0.128, 0.281, 0.243).
CLNPMI best only on 20News (0.174 vs CluHTM 0.164); TraCo higher on NIPS (0.054 vs 0.053) and nFNTM higher on Wikitext-103 (0.147 vs 0.145).
CluHTM did not converge within 48 hours on Wikitext-103.

strengths.text: Uses anchor words to give word-level guidance to hierarchy construction, improving both topic coherence and diversity across all three corpora.

limitations.text: External prior knowledge (e.g. ConceptNet) is not yet used to guide the anchor words.
Document metadata (author, tags, sentiment) is not combined with anchor words.
Cross-level coherence gains are not consistent: CLNPMI is second-best on two of three datasets.

notes: No code link found in the paper.
